transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and brought you in today?

I’ve been having trouble with little mistakes, mostly. I’ll think I’ve got something handled, but then I write the wrong time on a senior-center class sheet, or I measure a board and still cut it just a bit short because I missed the small print. It’s nothing huge, but it keeps happening enough that it’s bothering me.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have off days like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down or losing interest in things.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about making these mistakes, or do they keep coming back to your mind even when you're trying to focus on something else?
I don’t think I worry about it a lot, no. I might be annoyed when it happens, but it doesn’t keep playing over in my head or anything like that.
Have you noticed any difficulties with your memory or concentration lately, like forgetting things more often or having trouble focusing on tasks?

Yeah, mostly with concentration. Like at the senior center, if people are talking at the next table or my phone lights up, my mind kind of jumps over there. Then I lose my place in whatever I was filling out or building, and I have to back up and figure out where I was.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, hopeless, or have you taken less pleasure or interest in things you usually enjoy?
No, not really. I haven’t felt hopeless or lost interest in things. I’ve had normal bad days here and there, but nothing that stands out over the last couple weeks.
Have you had any days where you felt persistently down or where things just didn’t give you the same enjoyment as they used to, even if it wasn’t for a long time?
Not that I’ve noticed. I mean, I have an off day once in a while like anybody, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt persistently down or stopped enjoying things.
Do you find it hard to focus or maintain attention in other situations, like when you're reading, having a conversation, or watching something? Or is it mostly when there are distractions around you?

It’s mostly when there’s stuff going on around me. Like at the senior center, if people at the next table are talking, or my phone lights up, I kind of jump to that and then I’ve lost my place in what I was filling out or working on. Then I have to stop and figure out where I was again.
Outside of situations with distractions, do you ever find it hard to stay focused on things like reading, conversations, or tasks that require attention?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it as much when it’s quiet. If I’m by myself reading or doing something, I can usually stay with it better. The trouble seems to come up more when something pulls my attention away.
Do you remember having similar issues with distractions or trouble staying focused going back to when you were a child, or is this something that’s more recent?

Yeah, I think it goes back pretty far. Even in elementary school, I remember teachers saying I was bright, but they’d write things like I forgot my books or lost my homework. I’d also stare out the window unless somebody kept me on track. So it’s not brand new, no.
Have these issues with distractions and losing your place caused any significant problems for you, like at work, in relationships, or with daily tasks?

Yeah, a bit. It hasn’t ruined anything, but it has caused some problems. I stepped back from helping lead a couple of DIY workshops at the center because I was mixing things up and losing track. And at home, my wife tends to double-check plans now so I don’t mess up family visits or center activities. It’s frustrating, but I’d say it’s mild.
Do you find yourself getting distracted or losing focus in other parts of your life, like when you're at home, running errands, or somewhere other than the senior center?

Mostly I notice it at the senior center. Like if I’m filling something out or working on a project there and people start talking at the next table, or my phone lights up, my mind just jumps over to that. Then I lose my place in what I was doing.
Do you ever have trouble staying focused or get easily distracted in other places, like when you're at home, driving, or running errands, or is it mostly just at the senior center?

It’s mostly at the senior center that I notice it. If I’m filling out a form or building something and people start talking nearby, or my phone lights up, my attention just goes right to that and I lose my place.
Outside of the senior center, do you ever have trouble staying focused or get easily distracted when you're at home, driving, or running errands?

Not so much outside the senior center, no. That’s where I notice it most — if I’m filling something out or building something and people nearby are talking, or my phone lights up, I kind of jump over to that and lose my place.
